questions.stem: The festival 'Onam' is the harvest festival of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Onam is the major harvest festival of Kerala, celebrating the mythical homecoming of King Mahabali. It features the Vallam Kali (snake boat race), Pookalam (flower rangoli), Onam Sadya (feast), and Pulikali (tiger dance). It is celebrated in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August–September).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Bihu' is the chief festival of which state?
questions.explanation: Bihu is the chief festival of Assam, celebrated three times a year: Rongali/Bohag Bihu (spring, Assamese New Year, April), Kati/Kongali Bihu (autumn), and Magh/Bhogali Bihu (harvest, January). Rongali Bihu is the most important and features the energetic Bihu folk dance.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The harvest festival 'Pongal' is primarily celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: Pongal is the four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated in mid-January (corresponding to Makar Sankranti). The name comes from the dish 'pongal' (rice boiled with milk and jaggery). Its days are Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal (cattle), and Kaanum Pongal.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which festival is known as the 'Festival of Lights'?
questions.explanation: Diwali (Deepavali) is the 'Festival of Lights', celebrating the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. It marks Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana. Homes are lit with diyas, and it is celebrated across India in the month of Kartik (October–November). Holi is the festival of colours.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Baisakhi' is a harvest festival predominantly celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: Baisakhi (Vaisakhi), celebrated on 13/14 April, is the harvest festival of Punjab and also marks the Punjabi/Sikh New Year. It commemorates the founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699. It is celebrated with Bhangra and Giddha dances.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Hornbill Festival', a famous cultural festival, is celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in Nagaland (in December at Kisama), showcasing the culture of all major Naga tribes. Named after the hornbill bird featured in Naga folklore, it is called the 'Festival of Festivals' and promotes inter-tribal interaction and tourism.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The festival 'Bihu', 'Pongal', 'Makar Sankranti', and 'Lohri' share what common theme?

options.text: They all commemorate the birth of a deity
They are all harvest festivals celebrated around January
They are all observed only in South India

questions.explanation: Makar Sankranti (pan-India), Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Lohri (Punjab), and Magh Bihu (Assam) are all harvest festivals celebrated around mid-January, marking the sun's transition into Capricorn (Makara) and the end of the winter solstice period. They reflect India's agrarian gratitude for the harvest.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Rann Utsav', a cultural festival held in the white salt desert, is organised by which state?
questions.explanation: The Rann Utsav is a vibrant cultural festival organised by Gujarat in the white salt desert of the Rann of Kutch, typically from November to February. It showcases Kutchi handicrafts, folk music, dance, and the surreal landscape of the salt flats under the full moon.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Hemis Festival', celebrating Guru Padmasambhava, is held in which region?
questions.explanation: The Hemis Festival is celebrated at the Hemis Monastery in Ladakh, honouring the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche). It features the masked Cham dance performed by lamas. It is one of the most famous Buddhist festivals in the region.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The festival 'Bonalu' and 'Bathukamma' are floral/folk festivals of which state?
questions.explanation: Bonalu (honouring Goddess Mahakali) and Bathukamma (the floral festival of Goddess Gauri) are major folk festivals of Telangana. Bathukamma involves women arranging seasonal flowers in concentric layers and is celebrated during Navratri. Both are state festivals of Telangana.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which festival is celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of Lord Krishna?
questions.explanation: Janmashtami (Krishna Janmashtami / Gokulashtami) celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna. It is marked by fasting, midnight celebrations, and the 'Dahi Handi' tradition (forming human pyramids to break a pot of curd). Ram Navami marks Rama's birth; Ganesh Chaturthi marks Ganesha's.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Chhath Puja', dedicated to the Sun God, is most prominently celebrated in which states?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja is a major festival of Bihar, Jharkhand, and eastern Uttar Pradesh, dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya. Devotees offer 'arghya' to the setting and rising sun while standing in water, observing rigorous fasts. It is among the most physically demanding Hindu festivals.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The famous 'Rath Yatra' (chariot festival) is associated with which temple town?
questions.explanation: The Rath Yatra is the grand chariot festival of the Jagannath Temple at Puri, Odisha. The deities Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra are taken out in massive wooden chariots pulled by devotees. It is one of the oldest and largest such festivals, drawing huge crowds annually.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Losar' is the New Year festival celebrated by which community?
questions.explanation: Losar is the Tibetan Buddhist New Year, celebrated by communities in Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh (and Tibet). It involves prayers, mask dances, and feasting to welcome the new year and ward off evil spirits. The timing follows the Tibetan lunar calendar (around February).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The festival 'Wangala', celebrated by the Garo tribe, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Wangala is the post-harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya, honouring Saljong (the Sun God of fertility). It is also called the 'Hundred Drums Festival' for its rhythmic drumming. Meghalaya's three major tribes are the Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which festival marks the end of the holy month of Ramadan for Muslims?
questions.explanation: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan, the month of fasting. It is celebrated with special prayers, feasting, and giving of 'Zakat al-Fitr' (charity). Eid al-Adha (Bakrid) is the 'festival of sacrifice' commemorating Prophet Ibrahim; Muharram marks the Islamic New Year and the martyrdom of Imam Hussain.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Ganesh Chaturthi' festival is celebrated with greatest grandeur in which state?
questions.explanation: Ganesh Chaturthi (Vinayaka Chaturthi) is celebrated with the greatest grandeur in Maharashtra, where Lokmanya Tilak transformed it into a public festival during the freedom struggle to foster unity. Large idols of Lord Ganesha are installed and immersed (visarjan) after 1.5 to 11 days, famously at Mumbai's beaches.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Durga Puja', the grandest festival of West Bengal, celebrates:

options.text: Goddess Durga's victory over the demon Mahishasura

questions.explanation: Durga Puja celebrates Goddess Durga's victory over the buffalo-demon Mahishasura, symbolising the triumph of good over evil. The grandest festival of West Bengal (and also Odisha, Assam, Tripura), it features elaborate pandals and idols, ending with immersion (visarjan) on Vijayadashami. In 2021, Kolkata's Durga Puja was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Thrissur Pooram', famous for its caparisoned elephants and percussion ensembles, is celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: Thrissur Pooram is a spectacular temple festival of Kerala, held at the Vadakkunnathan Temple in Thrissur. It is renowned for its grand procession of caparisoned elephants, the 'Kudamattam' (umbrella display), and traditional percussion (Panchavadyam, Melam). It is often called the 'festival of festivals' of Kerala.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which festival celebrated in Kerala/Karnataka involves the worship of Lord Ayyappa and a pilgrimage to Sabarimala?
questions.explanation: Makaravilakku is the festival at Sabarimala (Kerala) associated with the pilgrimage to the shrine of Lord Ayyappa, culminating around Makar Sankranti when devotees witness the 'Makara Jyothi'. Vishu is the Malayalam New Year; Ugadi is the Telugu/Kannada New Year; Theyyam is a ritual dance form.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the New Year festival to its region. Which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Option D is INCORRECT. Bihu (specifically Rongali Bihu) is the New Year festival of ASSAM, not Kerala. Kerala's New Year is Vishu. The correct pairings: Ugadi (Karnataka/Andhra/Telangana), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Baisakhi (Punjab), Pohela Boishakh (Bengal), Vishu (Kerala) — all regional spring/solar new year festivals.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The festival 'Nuakhai', an agricultural/harvest festival, is celebrated primarily in which state?
questions.explanation: Nuakhai (Nuakhai Bhetghat) is an agricultural/harvest festival predominantly celebrated in western Odisha (and parts of neighbouring regions), where people welcome the new rice of the season ('nua' = new, 'khai' = eat). It is one of the most important social festivals of the Sambalpuri-speaking region.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Ziro Festival of Music' is held in which northeastern state?
questions.explanation: The Ziro Festival of Music is an outdoor music festival held in the Ziro Valley of Arunachal Pradesh, home to the Apatani tribe. Started in 2012, it has become one of India's most popular independent music festivals, set against scenic paddy fields. The Apatani cultural landscape is on UNESCO's tentative list.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which festival, celebrated mainly in Tamil Nadu and among Tamils, honours the deity Murugan and involves the carrying of 'Kavadi'?
questions.explanation: Thaipusam is a festival dedicated to Lord Murugan (Kartikeya), celebrated by Tamil communities (in India, Malaysia, Singapore). Devotees carry 'Kavadi' (decorated structures) and offer pots of milk, often as acts of penance. Karthigai Deepam is a festival of lights; Aadi Perukku is a Tamil monsoon/water festival.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Sangai Festival', named after a rare deer species, is the flagship tourism festival of which state?
questions.explanation: The Sangai Festival is the flagship tourism festival of Manipur, named after the Sangai (the brow-antlered 'dancing deer'), the state animal found in Keibul Lamjao National Park (the world's only floating national park, on Loktak Lake). The festival showcases Manipuri art, dance (Ras Leela), handloom, and cuisine.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
